evidence.quote: The survey collects self-reported metrics from software delivery teams across multiple industries, including technology, finance, healthcare, and retail.

After preprocessing (removal of incomplete responses and inconsistent entries), the final sample consists of N = 1,200 complete team-level observations. Data collection occurred between January and March 2024.
Second, one-way ANOVA was conducted to test for overall differences across the three cloud adoption levels. Following a significant ANOVA result, post-hoc Tukey HSD tests were performed
Third, multiple linear regression (OLS) was employed to estimate the marginal effect of cloud adoption on each performance metric while controlling team size.
the dataset overrepresents technology and finance sectors

Using the publicly available DORA Metrics dataset (N = 1,200 IT teams), we propose a linear regression model linking cloud adoption level (C) to four key performance indicators: deployment frequency (DF), lead time for changes (LT), mean time to recovery (MTTR), and change failure

cloud adoption positively predicted deployment frequency (β = 0.67, p < 0.001) and negatively predicted lead time (β = 0.54, p < 0.001), MTTR (β = -0.71, p < 0.001), and change failure rate (β = -0.48, p < 0.001).
Second, all metrics are self-reported, which may introduce social desirability or recall bias.
